questions.question: Who among the following novelists has written ‘A Suitable Boy’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Seth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vikram Seth** is an Indian author and poet known for his versatile writing.
 
• '**A Suitable Boy**' is one of his most renowned works, first published in 1993.
 
• The novel is set in post-independence, post-partition India and explores various social and political issues.
 
• 'A Suitable Boy' is one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume in the English language.
 
• The story revolves around a young girl's search for a suitable husband, intertwining various characters and subplots across India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vikram Seth's Other Works**

 
 
• '**The Golden Gate**' - A novel in verse form, published in 1986.
 
• '**An Equal Music**' - A novel published in 1999, exploring the lives of musicians.
 
• '**Two Lives**' - A non-fiction work published in 2005, detailing the lives of his great uncle and aunt.
 
 
 
• **A Suitable Boy's Adaptation**
 
 
• 'A Suitable Boy' was adapted into a television miniseries in 2020, directed by Mira Nair.
 
• The series was produced by the BBC and released on Netflix, featuring an ensemble cast.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**
 
 
• The novel is set in the early 1950s, a crucial period in India's history, post-independence.
 
• It reflects the socio-political landscape of the time, including land reforms and the rise of new political movements.
 
 
 
• **Literary Significance**
 
 
• 'A Suitable Boy' is celebrated for its detailed characterizations and intricate plot.
 
• The novel offers a panoramic view of Indian society and its complexities.

questions.question: Minati Mishra was conferred the Padma Shree for her contribution to which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Odissi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Minati Mishra was a renowned Indian classical dancer known for her contributions to the Odissi dance form.
 
• She was conferred the Padma Shree, one of India's highest civilian awards, in 2012 for her significant contributions to Odissi.
 
• Odissi is one of the oldest classical dance forms in India, originating from the state of Odisha.
 
• Minati Mishra was not only a performer but also a teacher and choreographer, contributing immensely to the promotion and preservation of Odissi.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Odissi Dance**:

 
 
• Odissi is characterized by its intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and sculpturesque poses.
 
• It is traditionally performed by women, and its themes are usually religious, often inspired by the Vaishnavism sect.
 
• Odissi is known for its Tribhangi posture, which divides the body into three parts: head, bust, and torso.
 
• The dance form includes both pure dance (Nritta) and expressive dance (Abhinaya).
 
 
 
• **Padma Shree Award**:
 
 
• The Padma Shree is the fourth highest civilian award in India.
 
• It is awarded to citizens of India in recognition of their distinguished contribution in various spheres of activity, including the arts.
 
• The award is announced on Republic Day (26th January) each year.
 
 
 
• **Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra**:
 
 
• He is considered one of the foremost exponents of Odissi dance.
 
• His contributions have been instrumental in reviving and popularizing the dance form in modern times.
 
 
 
• **Classical Dance Forms of India**:
 
 
• India is home to several classical dance forms, each with its unique style and cultural significance.
 
• Other major classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, and Sattriya.

questions.question: The Lakshmana temple of Khajuraho, dedicated to Lord Vishnu, is an example of which style of temple architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nagara**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lakshmana temple of Khajuraho, built during the Chandela dynasty, is dedicated to Lord Vishnu.
 
• The temple is an outstanding example of the Nagara style of temple architecture, which is prevalent in Northern India.
 
• The Nagara style is characterized by beehive-shaped towers known as 'shikharas'.
 
• The Lakshmana temple features a central shikhara that rises over the main sanctum (garbhagriha).
 
• Ornate carvings and intricate sculptures adorn the temple, depicting various mythological stories and deities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Architecture:**

 
 
• The Nagara style is one of the three main styles of temple architecture in India, the other two being Dravidian and Vesara.
 
• This style is primarily found in Northern and Central India and is characterized by its vertical elevation and curvilinear shikharas.
 
• Temples in the Nagara style often have a cruciform ground plan with several projections and recesses creating a complex pattern.
 
 
 
• **Khajuraho Group of Monuments:**
 
 
• The Khajuraho Group of Monuments is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• These temples were built between 950 and 1050 AD by the Chandela dynasty.
 
• They are famous for their stunning architectural symbolism and erotic sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Shikhara:**
 
 
• The shikhara is the tower or spire on top of a Hindu temple, which rises over the sanctum sanctorum (garbhagriha).
 
• In the Nagara style, the shikhara is typically a tall, curvilinear structure, symbolizing Mount Meru.
 
 
 
• **Garbhagriha:**
 
 
• The garbhagriha is the innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple where the primary deity is enshrined.
 
• It is considered the most sacred part of the temple and is usually a small, dark chamber.

questions.concept: External Sector and Currency Exchange rate
questions.question:
Consider the following methods adopted by the government to protect goods produced in India from imports.

(i) Heavy taxes were levied on imported goods

(ii) The maximum limit on the imports of a commodity by a domestic user was fixed Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Both (i) and (ii) are true**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Heavy taxes** on imported goods are commonly used by governments to protect domestic industries by making imported goods more expensive, thereby encouraging consumers to buy locally produced goods.
 
• **Import limits**, or quotas, are another method used to restrict the quantity of a specific commodity that can be imported, ensuring that domestic producers have a significant share of the market.
 
• Both of these measures are part of a broader strategy known as **protectionism**, aimed at safeguarding national economic interests.
 
• Protectionist policies are often adopted to help nascent industries develop without the pressure of international competition.
 
• These measures can help in boosting the local economy, increasing employment, and fostering the growth of domestic industries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tariffs:**

 
 
• Tariffs are taxes imposed by a government on goods and services imported from other countries, making them more expensive and less attractive compared to domestic products.
 
• They are used to restrict imports, raise government revenue, or protect domestic industries from foreign competition.
 
 
 
• **Quotas:**
 
 
• Quotas are limits set by a government on the amount of a specific product that can be imported over a set period of time.
 
• This method directly restricts the quantity of goods entering a country, thereby protecting domestic industries from excessive foreign competition.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies:**
 
 
• Subsidies are financial aids provided by the government to domestic industries to lower their production costs and make their products more competitive against imported goods.
 
• They can take various forms, such as direct cash payments, tax breaks, or low-interest loans.
 
 
 
• **Non-Tariff Barriers (NTBs):**
 
 
• NTBs include various regulations and standards imposed by a country to restrict imports without using tariffs, such as stringent quality standards, licensing requirements, and customs procedures.
 
• These barriers can significantly impact the volume of imports and protect domestic industries.

questions.question: Which of the following is a popular festival celebrated in the state of Bihar?

questions.question: Which region of India is known for the unique Shola forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Shola forests are a unique type of tropical montane forest found exclusively in the **Western Ghats** of India.
 
• These forests are characterized by their distinct mosaic of grasslands and stunted evergreen forests.
 
• The Shola forests are located at elevations ranging from 1,500 to 2,500 meters above sea level.
 
• They play a crucial role in preserving the biodiversity of the Western Ghats, which is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The Shola forests are vital for water conservation, as they are the source of many rivers and streams in the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**:

 
 
• The Western Ghats, also known as Sahyadri, is a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of the Indian peninsula.
 
• It is one of the eight "hottest hotspots" of biological diversity in the world.
 
• The Western Ghats extend over six states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• They are home to a variety of endemic species of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity**:
 
 
• Biodiversity refers to the variety and variability of life on Earth, encompassing the diversity within species, between species, and of ecosystems.
 
• Regions with high biodiversity, such as the Western Ghats, are crucial for maintaining ecological balance and providing ecosystem services.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site**:
 
 
• A World Heritage Site is a landmark or area with legal protection by an international convention administered by UNESCO.
 
• The Western Ghats were inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012 for their exceptional biodiversity and natural beauty.
 
 
 
• **Water Conservation**:
 
 
• Water conservation involves the strategies and activities to manage fresh water as a sustainable resource to protect the water environment and meet current and future human demand.
 
• The Shola forests contribute significantly to water conservation by acting as natural water reservoirs, feeding numerous rivers and streams.

questions.question: The Ghoomar dance of Rajasthan was originally performed by which tribal community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhil**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Ghoomar dance** is a traditional folk dance of Rajasthan.
 
• It was originally performed by the **Bhil tribal community** of Rajasthan.
 
• The dance is typically performed by women, who dance in circles and twirl while wearing colorful ghagras (long skirts).
 
• Ghoomar is often performed during auspicious occasions and festivals such as **Teej** and **Gangaur**.
 
• The dance is known for its graceful movements and intricate footwork.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History and Origin:**

 
 
• The Ghoomar dance originated from the Bhil tribe, which is one of the largest tribal communities in India.
 
• The dance was later adopted by other Rajasthani communities and became an integral part of Rajasthani culture.
 
 
 
• **Costumes and Music:**
 
 
• Participants wear traditional Rajasthani attire, including ghagras, cholis, and odhnis.
 
• The dance is accompanied by folk music featuring instruments like dhol, dholak, and harmonium.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Ghoomar is not just a dance but a social and cultural activity that brings communities together.
 
• It is performed to celebrate significant events such as weddings and festivals.
 
 
 
• **Recognition:**
 
 
• Ghoomar has gained international recognition and is performed at cultural events worldwide.
 
• It has been showcased in Bollywood films, further popularizing it.

questions.question: Who among the following was appointed as the first minister of the Ministry of Disinvestment during the tenure of the Vajpayee Government?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arun Shourie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Arun Shourie** was appointed as the first minister of the Ministry of Disinvestment.
 
• The Ministry of Disinvestment was created during the tenure of Prime Minister **Atal Bihari Vajpayee**.
 
• Arun Shourie held the position of Disinvestment Minister from **2000 to 2002**.
 
• He played a significant role in the disinvestment of public sector units, including **Bharat Aluminium Company (BALCO)** and **Hindustan Zinc**.
 
• His tenure is noted for the initiation of major disinvestment policies in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ministry of Disinvestment**:

 
 
• The Ministry of Disinvestment was established in **1999** during the Vajpayee Government.
 
• The primary objective was to oversee the disinvestment of government stakes in public sector enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment**:
 
 
• Disinvestment involves the sale of government-owned assets or stakes in public sector enterprises to private entities.
 
• It aims to reduce the financial burden on the government and improve the efficiency of these enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Bharat Aluminium Company (BALCO)**:
 
 
• BALCO was one of the first major public sector enterprises to be privatized in 2001.
 
• The government sold a 51% stake in BALCO to Sterlite Industries.
 
 
 
• **Hindustan Zinc**:
 
 
• Hindustan Zinc, a leading producer of zinc, was also disinvested during Arun Shourie’s tenure.
 
• A significant stake was sold to Sterlite Industries, making it the largest private shareholder.

questions.question: Which of the following dances was traditionally performed by male monks in monasteries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India that originated in the state of Assam.
 
• This dance was traditionally performed by **male monks** in the **Vaishnavite monasteries** called **Sattras**.
 
• **Sattriya** dance was introduced in the 15th century by the saint-scholar **Sankardev** as a medium for **religious expression and devotion**.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **spiritual themes**, including tales from the life of Lord Krishna and other religious stories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sankardev**:

 
 
• He was a 15th-16th century saint-scholar, poet, playwright, and social-religious reformer in Assam.
 
• Sankardev is credited with the creation and propagation of the **Neo-Vaishnavite movement** in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Sattras**:
 
 
• Sattras are **Vaishnavite monasteries** that were established by Sankardev and his followers to promote the Neo-Vaishnavite culture and religion.
 
• These institutions are centers of religious, cultural, and educational activities in Assam.
 
 
 
• **Other Classical Dances of India**:
 
 
• **Kathakali**: A classical dance form from Kerala known for its elaborate costumes and dramatic performances.
 
• **Kuchipudi**: A classical dance from Andhra Pradesh, known for its graceful movements and strong narrative character.
 
• **Odissi**: A classical dance form from Odisha, characterized by its sculpturesque poses and fluid movements.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism**:
 
 
• It is one of the major traditions within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, primarily Rama and Krishna.
 
• Vaishnavism emphasizes the devotion (bhakti) towards Vishnu as the Supreme God.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India mentions that Parliament by law can form a new State by separation of territory from any state or by uniting any territory to a part of any State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 3** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Parliament to form a new state by separation of territory from any state or by uniting any territories to a part of any state.
 
• The Parliament can also increase or diminish the area of any state, alter the boundaries or the name of any state under **Article 3**.
 
• Before introducing a bill under Article 3, the President must refer it to the state legislature concerned for expressing its views within a specified period.
 
• However, the Parliament can pass the bill with or without accepting the views of the state legislature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 2** provides the Parliament the power to admit or establish new states into the Union of India.
 
• **Article 4** states that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for the formation of new states are not to be considered amendments under Article 368.
 
• The process of altering state boundaries is essential for administrative efficiency and socio-economic development.
 
• Article 3 ensures the federal structure of India is maintained while allowing for flexibility in state reorganization.
 
• Some notable instances of state reorganization include the formation of states like Telangana (2014) and Uttarakhand (2000).

questions.question: According to the census of India 2011, what was the literacy rate of Tamil Nadu?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the several approaches of microfinance delivery mechanisms in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cheap subsidised credit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Cheap subsidized credit is not considered an official approach of microfinance delivery mechanisms in India.
 
• Microfinance delivery mechanisms in India typically involve structured programs like Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and Microfinance Institutions (MFIs).
 
• These mechanisms focus on providing financial services to low-income groups, aiming at financial inclusion and poverty alleviation.
 
• Subsidized credit schemes generally fall under broader financial inclusion initiatives but are not categorized specifically under microfinance delivery mechanisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self-Help Groups (SHGs) - Bank Linkage Programme**:

 
 
• Launched by NABARD in 1992, this program links informal groups of women to banks for financial assistance.
 
• SHGs serve as a significant model for poverty alleviation, women's empowerment, and financial inclusion.
 
 
 
• **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs) - Credit Lending Models**:
 
 
• MFIs provide financial services to low-income groups, including small loans, savings accounts, and insurance.
 
• They operate under various models like joint liability groups, individual lending, and cooperative societies.
 
 
 
• **Conventional Weaker-Section Lending by Banks**:
 
 
• Banks are mandated to lend a portion of their portfolios to weaker sections, including small farmers, artisans, and other low-income groups.
 
• This includes priority sector lending targets set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
 
 
• **Microfinance**:
 
 
• Microfinance refers to the provision of financial services to low-income individuals or groups who are typically excluded from traditional banking.
 
• It includes credit, savings, insurance, and remittance services aimed at fostering economic growth and self-sufficiency.

questions.question: Under which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India does the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh have special responsibility with respect to law and order and in discharge of his functions in relation thereto?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 371 H**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 371 H** of the Indian Constitution grants special powers to the Governor of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Under this Article, the Governor has special responsibility with respect to law and order in the state.
 
• The Governor, in the discharge of his functions in relation to law and order, has the discretion to act according to his judgment.
 
• This provision was included to address the unique socio-political and security challenges in Arunachal Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 371** of the Indian Constitution contains a series of special provisions for various states in India to address their unique needs and challenges.
 
• **Article 371 A** pertains to special provisions with respect to the state of Nagaland, granting autonomy in religious or social practices, customary law, and administration of civil and criminal justice involving decisions according to Naga customary law.
 
• **Article 371 D** deals with special provisions for the state of Andhra Pradesh, particularly concerning equitable opportunities and facilities in public employment and education for people from different parts of the state.
 
• **Article 371 G** provides special provisions for the state of Mizoram, similar to those in Article 371 A for Nagaland, focusing on preserving the religious and social practices of the Mizos.

questions.question: Which of the following words is not part of Article 15 of the Indian Constitution as far as grounds of discrimination are concerned?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Profession**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 15 of the Indian Constitution prohibits discrimination on the grounds of **religion, race, caste, sex, and place of birth**.
 
• The term "profession" is not mentioned in Article 15 as a ground for discrimination.
 
• This article ensures that every citizen has equal access to public places and institutions, irrespective of the specified grounds.
 
• The provision also extends to the state, ensuring that no citizen is discriminated against in the matter of public employment or office under the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 14:**

 
 
• Ensures equality before the law and equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
 
• It prohibits any discrimination by the state against any person.
 
 
 
• **Article 16:**
 
 
• Provides for equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
 
• No citizen can be discriminated against in respect of employment or office under the state on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex, descent, place of birth, residence or any of them.
 
 
 
• **Article 17:**
 
 
• Abolishes "untouchability" and forbids its practice in any form.
 
• It is a direct outcome of the principle of equality enshrined in the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Article 18:**
 
 
• Abolishes titles and makes it a punishable offense to confer or accept any title, except military or academic distinctions.

questions.question: Which common long-term infection develops when bacteria in the mouth metabolise sugars to produce acids that demineralise the hard tissues of teeth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dental caries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dental caries**, also known as tooth decay or cavities, is a common long-term infection caused by the activity of bacteria in the mouth.
 
• Bacteria such as *Streptococcus mutans* metabolise sugars from food to produce acids.
 
• The produced acids lead to the demineralisation and destruction of the hard tissues of the teeth, primarily the enamel and dentin.
 
• Dental caries can develop into pain, tooth loss, and infection if left untreated.
 
• Preventive measures include maintaining good oral hygiene, reducing sugar intake, and regular dental check-ups.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Demineralisation:**

 
 
• Demineralisation is the process where minerals like calcium and phosphate are removed from the tooth enamel by acids produced by bacteria.
 
• This process weakens the tooth structure and makes it more susceptible to decay.
 
 
 
• **Streptococcus mutans:**
 
 
• Streptococcus mutans is a type of bacteria that plays a significant role in the development of dental caries.
 
• It adheres to the tooth surface and produces lactic acid as a by-product of sugar metabolism.
 
 
 
• **Fluoride:**
 
 
• Fluoride is a mineral that helps in remineralisation, strengthening the tooth enamel, and making it more resistant to acid attacks.
 
• It is commonly found in toothpaste and public water supplies.
 
 
 
• **Preventive Dentistry:**
 
 
• Preventive dentistry involves practices that help maintain oral health and prevent dental caries, such as regular brushing, flossing, and professional cleanings.
 
• It also includes dietary recommendations to reduce sugar intake and the application of dental sealants.
 
 
 
• **Enamel:**
 
 
• Enamel is the hard, outer layer of the tooth that protects it from decay and damage.
 
• Once enamel is eroded by acids, it cannot regenerate, making preventive measures crucial.

questions.question: In which part of the Constitution of India is the procedure for amendments in the Constitution laid down?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The procedure for amendments in the Constitution of India is laid down in **Part XX** of the Constitution.
 
• **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution specifically deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• An amendment can be initiated only by the introduction of a Bill for the purpose in either House of Parliament.
 
• The Bill must be passed in each House by a majority of the total membership of that House and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members of that House present and voting.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Significant Amendments:**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, known as the "Mini-Constitution," brought about widespread changes.
 
• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978, reversed many provisions of the 42nd Amendment.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**

• The landmark case of Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) established the Basic Structure Doctrine, limiting Parliament's power to amend the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Amendment Process:**

• The tropopause is the boundary layer between the troposphere and the stratosphere.
 
• At the equator, the tropopause is located at an altitude of about 17 to 18 kilometers (55,000 to 60,000 feet).
 
• The air temperature at the tropopause over the equator is approximately -80ºC.
 
• This temperature is significantly lower than at the Earth's surface due to the decrease in temperature with altitude in the troposphere.
 
• The temperature at the tropopause varies with latitude and season, but it is generally coldest at the equator.

• **Tropopause**:

 
 
• The tropopause marks the top of the troposphere and the beginning of the stratosphere.
 
• It acts as a barrier to the mixing of tropospheric and stratospheric air.
 
 
 
• **Temperature Gradient**:
 
 
• The troposphere features a negative temperature gradient, meaning temperature decreases with altitude.
 
• In the stratosphere above the tropopause, the temperature increases with altitude.
 
 
 
• **Equatorial Tropopause**:
 
 
• The equatorial tropopause is higher and colder compared to the tropopause at higher latitudes.
 
• This is due to the intense solar heating in the equatorial region, leading to a higher convection and altitude of the tropopause.
 
 
 
• **Stratospheric Temperature**:
 
 
• The stratosphere, just above the tropopause, contains the ozone layer which absorbs UV radiation, causing a temperature increase with altitude.
 
• This positive temperature gradient in the stratosphere contrasts with the negative gradient in the troposphere.

questions.question: To which genus does the nematode parasite called hookworm belong, which usually spreads through infected soil?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ancylostoma**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ancylostoma** is the genus to which the hookworm parasite belongs.
 
• Hookworms are nematode parasites that infect the intestines of their hosts.
 
• They are primarily spread through contact with infected soil, where the larvae can penetrate the skin.
 
• Common species of hookworms in the Ancylostoma genus include *Ancylostoma duodenale* and *Ancylostoma caninum*.
 
• Infections can lead to conditions such as anemia and protein deficiency due to blood loss.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hookworm Life Cycle:**

 
 
• Eggs are passed in the feces of an infected host.
 
• Larvae hatch in the soil and can survive for several weeks.
 
• Infective larvae penetrate the skin of humans, typically through bare feet.
 
• Larvae migrate through the bloodstream to the lungs, are coughed up, swallowed, and mature in the intestines.
 
 
 
• **Symptoms of Hookworm Infection:**
 
 
• Symptoms can include abdominal pain, diarrhea, weight loss, fatigue, and anemia.
 
• Severe infections can lead to significant blood loss and nutritional deficiencies.
 
 
 
• **Prevention and Control:**
 
 
• Wearing shoes to avoid contact with contaminated soil.
 
• Proper sanitation and disposal of human feces.
 
• Periodic deworming in endemic areas.
 
 
 
• **Treatment:**
 
 
• Anthelmintic medications such as albendazole or mebendazole are commonly used.
 
• Supplemental iron may be needed to address anemia.

questions.question: Under which of the following Acts can supreme court initiate International Commercial Arbitration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996**__.

__
 
• The Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 governs arbitration proceedings in India, including international commercial arbitration.
 
• This Act is based on the UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration, reflecting international standards.
 
• It provides a comprehensive framework for both domestic and international arbitration, ensuring that disputes are resolved efficiently.
 
• The Supreme Court of India can initiate and enforce arbitration under this Act, ensuring that arbitration agreements are upheld and arbitral awards are executed.
 
• The Act has been amended several times, most recently in 2019, to enhance its efficiency and transparency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNCITRAL Model Law:**

 
 
• The UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration was adopted by the United Nations Commission on International Trade Law (UNCITRAL) in 1985.
 
• It aims to assist countries in reforming and modernizing their arbitration laws to ensure uniformity and fairness in the resolution of international commercial disputes.
 
• The Model Law provides a framework that nations can adopt to ensure that their arbitration laws are aligned with international standards.
 
 
 
• **Arbitration Agreement:**
 
 
• An arbitration agreement is a written agreement between parties to submit their disputes to arbitration instead of going to court.
 
• Such agreements are typically included in commercial contracts to ensure that any future disputes are resolved through arbitration.
 
 
 
• **Arbitral Award:**
 
 
• An arbitral award is the decision made by an arbitrator or arbitral tribunal in an arbitration proceeding.
 
• It is binding on the parties involved and can be enforced in the same manner as a court judgment.
 
 
 
• **International Commercial Arbitration:**
 
 
• International commercial arbitration is a method of resolving disputes arising out of international commercial transactions.
 
• It involves parties from different countries and is governed by international treaties and conventions, such as the New York Convention.

questions.question: ‘The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn’ was written by which of the following authors?

• **Mark Twain** is the pen name of Samuel Langhorne Clemens, an American writer and humorist born on November 30, 1835.
 
• Twain is best known for his novels "The Adventures of Tom Sawyer" (1876) and "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" (1884), the latter often called "The Great American Novel."
 
• "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" is recognized for its vivid descriptions of people and places along the Mississippi River.
 
• Mark Twain's writing is noted for its humor, social criticism, and portrayal of American culture and values during the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• "The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn" addresses themes of race, identity, and morality, offering a critical view of the pre-Civil War South.
 
• Twain’s works often critique societal norms and injustices, making them relevant to both his time and modern discussions.
 
 
 
• **Influence:**

questions.question: Simuka was the founder of which of the following dynasties of the post Mauryan era?

• The Satavahana dynasty is also known as the **Andhra dynasty**.
 
• Simuka's reign is believed to have begun around **230 BCE** and lasted until **207 BCE**.
 
• The Satavahanas are known for their significant contributions to **Indian culture, trade, and administration**.
 
• The Satavahana dynasty ruled a substantial part of central and southern India, including modern-day Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Andhra Pradesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Satavahana Administration:**

 
 
• The Satavahana rulers followed a well-organized administrative structure, with provinces called **Janapadas**.
 
• Their administration was marked by the use of **Prakrit language** and inscriptions in the Brahmi script.
 
 
 
• **Trade and Economy:**
 
 
• The Satavahanas played a crucial role in **maritime trade**, establishing trade links with the Roman Empire and Southeast Asia.
 
• They issued a large number of **coins** made of lead, copper, and silver, facilitating commerce.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Contributions:**
 
 
• The Satavahana period saw the flourishing of **Buddhist art and architecture**, including the construction of stupas and viharas.

• The Satavahana dynasty gradually declined by the 3rd century CE, with its territories being taken over by emerging regional powers like the **Ikshvakus** and the **Vakatakas**.

• The Green Revolution involved the introduction of high-yielding varieties (HYVs) of seeds, especially for wheat and rice, which significantly increased agricultural production in India.
 
• It included the widespread use of chemical fertilizers and pesticides to enhance crop yield and protect plants from pests and diseases.
 
• Advanced irrigation techniques, such as tube wells and water pumps, were introduced to ensure a consistent water supply, reducing dependency on monsoon rains.
 
• The adoption of modern agricultural practices and machinery, such as tractors and harvesters, helped in reducing manual labor and increasing efficiency in farming operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High-Yielding Varieties (HYVs)**:

 
 
• HYVs are seeds engineered to produce more grain per plant, which was a key component of the Green Revolution.
 
• These seeds were more responsive to chemical fertilizers and irrigation, leading to increased productivity.
 
 
 
• **Chemical Fertilizers and Pesticides**:
 
 
• The use of chemical fertilizers like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium (NPK) played a crucial role in enhancing soil fertility and crop growth.
 
• Pesticides helped in controlling pests and diseases, ensuring healthier crops and higher yields.

• Efficient irrigation methods, such as drip irrigation and sprinkler systems, were introduced to optimize water usage.

• **Impact on Food Security**:
 
 
• The Green Revolution significantly improved food security in India, transforming the country from a food-deficient nation to a self-sufficient one.

questions.question: Which of the following is involved in the movement of lava over or towards the surface of the earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Volcanism**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Volcanism** refers to the process through which magma (lava) is expelled from beneath the Earth's crust to its surface.
 
• This process is primarily responsible for the formation of volcanic landforms such as mountains, islands, and plateaus.
 
• Volcanism involves the eruption of molten rock, gases, and ash from a volcano, which can occur explosively or effusively.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the recycling of the Earth's crust and the release of gases from the interior to the atmosphere.
 
• The movement of lava over the Earth's surface can create new land and significantly alter existing landscapes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weathering**:

 
 
• Weathering is the process of breaking down rocks, soil, and minerals through direct contact with the Earth's atmosphere, water, and biological organisms.
 
• It is a gradual process that does not involve the movement of lava.
 
 
 
• **Exogenic Processes**:
 
 
• Exogenic processes are external processes such as erosion, weathering, and sedimentation that shape the Earth's surface.
 
• These processes are driven by external forces like wind, water, and ice.
 
 
 
• **Diastrophism**:
 
 
• Diastrophism refers to the deformation of the Earth's crust due to tectonic forces, leading to the formation of features such as mountains and faults.
 
• It does not involve the movement of lava but rather the movement of the Earth's crust.
 
 
 
• **Types of Volcanic Eruptions**:
 
 
• **Effusive Eruptions**: Characterized by the outpouring of lava onto the ground.
 
• **Explosive Eruptions**: Involves violent explosions that eject ash, gas, and rock fragments into the air.
 
• Both types of eruptions are part of the process of volcanism.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims to provide generic medicines at reasonable prices to the citizen of the country?

• They are typically sold at lower prices than branded medicines.
 
• The use of generic medicines can significantly reduce healthcare costs for both individuals and healthcare systems.

questions.question: Devadasi National Award is given at the dance festival held at the pilgrim centre in the state of _________.

questions.question: Who among the following emphasised and propagated that “the Vedanta is the religion of all and not of the Hindus alone”?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekanand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Swami Vivekananda was an Indian Hindu monk and a chief disciple of the 19th-century Indian mystic Ramakrishna.
 
• He is best known for his speech which began with "Sisters and brothers of America ...," at the Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago in 1893.
 
• Swami Vivekananda emphasized that the Vedanta philosophy could serve as a universal religion.
 
• He believed that Vedanta is not confined to Hinduism but is a science of spirituality that transcends all religions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vedanta:**

 
 
• Vedanta is one of the six orthodox schools of Hindu philosophy.
 
• It is based on the teachings of the Upanishads, which are a collection of ancient Sanskrit texts that expound on the nature of reality and the self.
 
• Vedanta emphasizes the idea of Brahman (the ultimate reality) and Atman (the individual soul), and their unity.
 
 
 
• **Ramakrishna Mission:**
 
 
• Founded by Swami Vivekananda in 1897, the mission aims to promote the teachings of Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.
 
• It focuses on religious and social service, including education, health care, and relief efforts.
 
 
 
• **Parliament of the World's Religions:**
 
 
• The first Parliament was held in Chicago in 1893.
 
• It is considered a landmark event for interfaith dialogue.
 
• Swami Vivekananda's address at this event brought him international recognition.
 
 
 
• **Universal Religion:**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda's concept of a universal religion is based on the idea that all religions are different paths leading to the same goal.
 
• He believed that Vedanta could serve as a foundation for a universal religion, promoting harmony and peace among different faiths.

questions.question: What is the spread of living pteridophytes to narrow geographical regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Limited and restricted**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pteridophytes, commonly known as ferns and their relatives, exhibit a **limited and restricted distribution** in specific geographical regions.
 
• These plants are generally found in **moist and shaded environments**, such as tropical and temperate forests.
 
• Their spread is restricted due to their **requirement for water** for fertilization, which limits their habitat range.
 
• Many species of pteridophytes are **endemic**, meaning they are native to and found only in specific regions.
 
• Factors such as **climatic conditions, soil type, and altitude** play significant roles in determining the distribution of pteridophytes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pteridophytes** are a group of vascular plants that reproduce via spores and do not produce seeds or flowers.
 
• They are considered to be the **first true vascular plants** and include ferns, horsetails, clubmosses, and whisk ferns.
 
• **Endemism** refers to species that are native to a particular geographical region and are not naturally found elsewhere.
 
• Pteridophytes have significant ecological roles, including **soil formation, nutrient cycling, and providing habitats** for other organisms.
 
• These plants are also important in studies of plant evolution and biodiversity due to their ancient origins and diverse forms.

questions.question: The Rigveda Samhita comprises of _____ books.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rigveda Samhita is divided into ten books, also known as Mandalas.
 
• These ten Mandalas are further classified into two groups: the Family Books (Mandalas 2-7) and the remaining books (Mandalas 1, 8-10).
 
• The Family Books are considered the oldest part of the Rigveda.
 
• The Rigveda is one of the four sacred texts (Vedas) of ancient India, composed in Vedic Sanskrit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rigveda**:

 
 
• The Rigveda is one of the oldest known texts in any Indo-European language.
 
• It comprises hymns dedicated to various deities, including Indra, Agni, and Soma.
 
• The Rigveda is an important source for understanding the early Vedic culture and religion.
 
 
 
• **Vedic Literature**:
 
 
• Vedic literature is divided into four main collections: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• Each Veda has four parts: Samhitas (hymns), Brahmanas (rituals), Aranyakas (theological discussions), and Upanishads (philosophical teachings).
 
 
 
• **Mandalas**:
 
 
• Each Mandala in the Rigveda is a collection of hymns or mantras.
 
• The Mandalas are not of uniform length; some are significantly longer than others.
 
• They are traditionally attributed to various ancient rishis (sages).
 
 
 
• **Language and Composition**:
 
 
• The hymns of the Rigveda were composed in Vedic Sanskrit, an ancient form of the Sanskrit language.
 
• The composition of the Rigveda is believed to have occurred over several centuries.

questions.question: Which of the following states had the least decadal growth in literacy rate, as per census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1) Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mizoram recorded the **least decadal growth** in literacy rate among Indian states as per the Census 2011.
 
• The literacy rate in Mizoram increased from **88.8%** in 2001 to **91.6%** in 2011, marking a growth of **2.8%**.
 
• In contrast, other states such as Tripura and Kerala showed higher decadal growth rates in literacy.
 
• Mizoram's high base literacy rate in 2001 contributed to the smaller percentage increase over the decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate Definition:**

 
 
• The literacy rate is defined as the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding in any language.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• The Census 2011 is the 15th National Census survey conducted by the Government of India.
 
• It provides comprehensive data on various demographic parameters including literacy rates.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Literacy:**
 
 
• Kerala had the highest literacy rate in India as per Census 2011, with a literacy rate of 94%.
 
• Kerala's focused educational policies have historically contributed to its high literacy rates.
 
 
 
• **Tripura's Literacy Growth:**
 
 
• Tripura saw a significant increase in its literacy rate, from 73.2% in 2001 to 87.2% in 2011, marking a growth of 14%.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Literacy:**
 
 
• Higher literacy rates contribute to economic growth, poverty reduction, and improved health outcomes.
 
• Literacy empowers individuals and enhances their ability to participate fully in societal activities.

questions.question: Who advises the Governor with respect to proroguing of the session of the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on proroguing the session of the State Legislature.
 
• Proroguing refers to the ending of a session of the legislature, after which a new session may be convened.
 
• This advice is given by the Chief Minister as part of their executive role in the state government.
 
• The Governor acts on this advice in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Legislature:**

 
 
• The State Legislature consists of the Governor and one or two houses, as per the state's constitution.
 
• In states with bicameral legislatures, there is a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
 
 
• **Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor's role includes summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the State Legislature on the advice of the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Proroguing:**
 
 
• Proroguing is the termination of a session of the legislature without dissolving it.
 
• It results in the adjournment of all pending legislative business until the next session.
 
 
 
• **Executive Role of Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and leads the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on various matters, including legislative sessions, state policy, and administration.
